Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the demo last week. Per our procurement checklist, attaching our current subprocessor roster and a set of DPA redlines the Acme legal team would like Redwood to review. Key asks from our side: a clear notification window for new subprocessors, an objection mechanism for high-risk subprocessors, and confirmation of the execution route (DocuSign preferred).

Attachments: acme_subprocessor_list_2027-01-15.csv (CSV, 2 pages), redlines_acme_dpa_comments.pdf (PDF)

Quick summary:
- Proposed notification window: 60 days prior notice for new subprocessors
- Objection path: customer can object on security/compliance grounds; want escalation contacts and escalation SLA
- Execution: can Redwood accept DocuSign envelope with a wholesale redline set?

Please let us know who on Redwood legal should be the primary contact. Happy to set a short call to walk through the redlines if helpful.

Best,

Hi Alice — thanks for sending this over and for the clear summary. Looping in Rishi (security) and Karthik (legal/sales). A few quick notes from our side:

- Redwood standard notification window is 30 days for low-impact subprocessors and 45 days for high-impact ones. We can evaluate a 60-day ask for extremely high-risk categories but would like to understand which vendors you consider high-risk on the attached CSV.
- Objection mechanism: we support a documented objection path with an escalation ladder (customer -> Redwood Security -> Redwood Legal -> joint remediation plan) and a 30-day cure period before remedial action. We can propose language for the DPA.
- Execution: DocuSign is acceptable; we use DocuSign for most enterprise DPAs. We need the final redline file in Word format (track changes preferred) to import into our e-sign workflow.

Could you flag the 3–5 vendors you consider critical/high-risk in the attached CSV and confirm whether your procurement team requires any specific audit artifacts (SOC2 type II, ISO, penetration test reports)?

If you prefer, we can do a 30-minute sync next week to go through the CSV and the redlines.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Partnerships

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Subprocessor list + DPA redlines for Redwood (for legal review)

Hi Alice — thanks for the detailed update and for marking the high-risk vendors. I've reviewed the Word redlines and propose the following path forward: 

1) Notification windows:
- Agree to 60-day notification for changes that affect EU personal data or data residency shifts (we'll mark this as an exception in the DPA).
- Standard 45-day prior notice for other high-impact subprocessors; 30 days for routine additions.

2) Objection & remediation:
- Proposed objection process: customer submits written objection within 30 days of notice, Redwood responds within 10 business days with either mitigation plan or rationale. If unresolved, escalate to joint technical review and remediation plan with a 30-day cure period.

3) Execution workflow:
- We can accept DocuSign. Operational notes: please ensure the final Word redline is the source of truth; our contracts system will import the Word file and generate a DocuSign envelope. If Acme needs a separate signer (two-step procurement + legal sign), indicate that at signing time and include signer emails in the envelope request.

4) Evidence requests:
- For IdentityBridge and EU-Logix, Redwood security requests SOC2 Type II report and the latest external penetration test summary before the objection cure period ends. We can accept secure-drive links (limited-time access) or vendor-signed attestations.

Action items: Naomi, can you confirm internal approval on the 60-day exception for EU/residency and confirm whether we need to surface this to leadership for one-off sign-off? Laura, please chime in on procurement timing and whether we should offer a short-term indemnity/hold harmless language while evidence is gathered.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel (Contracts)
Redwood Inference

Karthik / Naomi — I support the exception path for 60 days for EU/residency impact, provided Security (Rishi) signs off on the specific evidence requirements listed. Procurement timeline note: if Acme needs both procurement and legal signatures, that will add ~3 business days to our turnaround because we route the envelope to two internal signers. We should tell Acme to expect ~5 business days total after we receive the final Word redline and evidence links.

Also request we include a short data residency clause (one sentence) referencing the locations in the CSV and confirming Redwood will not move EU customer data outside EU without notice. Karthik — please add that clause in your next redline.

Laura Bennett
